quiz.q: According to Hegemonic Stability Theory, why does a liberal economic order require a hegemon?
options: An open trade order cannot emerge or survive automatically without a dominant power managing it.
States naturally cooperate to eliminate protectionist trade barriers without requiring any external enforcement.
Free-riding allies spontaneously provide global public goods once international trade disputes are resolved.
Military alliances alone suffice to prevent economic protectionism without needing centralized economic leadership.
quiz.why: Kindleberger and Gilpin argue that a liberal economic order does not emerge on its own and must be created and managed by a hegemon.

quiz.q: How does Fareed Zakaria explain the emergence of what he terms the 'post-American world'?
options: It is driven by excessive American reliance on hard power during the Bush administration.
It results from a complete diffusion of power creating an unstable world without polarity.
It stems from a deliberate policy choice that future administrations can easily reverse.
It has occurred due to the rise of other nations rather than American domestic overstretch.
quiz.why: Zakaria argues that the post-American world has emerged not because America overstretched itself, but because of the rise of other nations.

quiz.q: What strategy does Henry Kissinger recommend for managing the rise of China?
options: Strict containment aimed at preserving the existing power gap between both nations.
Respectful diplomatic engagement that addresses China's genuine grievances as an opportunity.
Imposing aggressive unilateral tariffs to eliminate the bilateral trade deficit immediately.
Terminating economic interdependence to prevent falling into a Thucydides trap.
quiz.why: Kissinger argues that the United States should treat China respectfully, address its genuine grievances, and pursue engagement rather than containment.

quiz.q: Which structural factor do scholars highlight to argue that China poses no immediate threat to US hegemony?
options: China possesses a completely self-contained economy that rejects international multilateral financial institutions.
China has successfully closed the soft power and technological gap with the United States.
China will grow old before becoming big while the United States maintains a demographic dividend.
China enjoys a tranquil and secure regional periphery free from any territorial border disputes.
quiz.why: Scholars argue that China will age before it becomes big, while the United States benefits from a demographic dividend, superior technology, and greater soft power.
